summary: Comb next-state logic for inputs_invalid sticky error flags with per-operation enable gating and a synchronous clear.
behavior: The block computes the next value of the inputs_invalid flag vector (inputs_invalid_d). By default it holds the current state (inputs_invalid_q). When clr_err is asserted, all flags are cleared to zero. Otherwise, when valid is active, four operation-specific flags (OpAdvance, OpGenId, OpGenSwOut, OpGenHwOut) are updated: each flag is set to 1 only if the corresponding operation enable (adv_en_i for advance, id_en_i for generate ID, gen_en_i for software and hardware output generation) is high AND either the input-stage invalid indicator (inputs_invalid_i) or the currently latched invalid indicator (inputs_invalid_q) is already set. This creates sticky error flags that, once set, remain high across cycles (as long as valid toggles and the enable remains high) until explicitly cleared by clr_err.

guarantees.property: Asserting clr_err forces inputs_invalid_d to all-zero immediately (combinational path).

security_implications: The inputs_invalid flags are part of the key manager’s input validation; stuck flags prevent propagation of invalid operation requests until explicitly cleared. The logic ensures that an erroneous operation (detected as inputs_invalid_i) and its past occurrence are remembered, which is essential for safe sequencing and avoiding unauthorized key material generation.
uncertain_points: Whether valid and the enable signals are guaranteed to be mutually exclusive or can overlap across different operation types is not specified here – the logic permits simultaneous setting of multiple flags if respective enables are high and the input/state invalid bits are set.
